sections.html:
Locals call Independence the Queen City of the Trails, since wagons left from here on the California, Oregon and Santa Fe Trails. The town was founded March 29, 1827, and sits on the south bank of the Missouri River and is the largest suburb on the Missouri side of the Kansas City area. Harry Truman grew up here, and the Truman Library and Museum and the Truman National Historic Site are in town.

The 2020 census counted 123,011 residents, making it the fifth-largest city in Missouri. Most of the city is in Jackson County, and a small part extends into Clay County. ZIP codes run from 64050 through 64058.

Independence spreads over 78 square miles, and about 61% of its homes are owner-occupied.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,387, and owners without one report $593. The mean commute is 23.9 minutes, and 89.2% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. The 2025 estimate is 1.0% below the 2020 base, so the city is shrinking slightly.

Every residential rental unit in Independence needs a city license and must pass an inspection before it can be leased. The Rental Ready program started June 1, 2017. The council expanded it in January 2025 from nine inspection items to sixteen, and the new rules took effect May 1, 2025.

The inspection costs $100 per dwelling unit, and a failed unit pays $60 for reinspection. Each unit is inspected every two years or at a change of tenant, and never more than four years apart. In buildings with five or more units, half the units are inspected, and they cannot be ones inspected before. A city-approved private inspector does the work. Landlord licenses run for one year and renew annually.

Since January 1, 2026, a tenant cannot start utility service for a rental unless the landlord holds a valid, active business license. If you are selling a rental house, hand the buyer your license number and your most recent inspection result.

  • The sixteen items include electrical systems, smoke detectors, handrails, plumbing fixtures, hot and cold water, GFCI outlets, egress, heating, furnaces and water heaters, and window fall protection.
  • Tenants who want the city to act must first notify the landlord, who has seven days to respond.
  • Questions go to Business and Landlord Licensing at (816) 325-7079 or blicenses@indepmo.org.

sections.h2: Code violations owners get cited for
sections.html:
Chapters 4 and 14 of the city code are enforced by the Property Maintenance Division, which usually lets an owner fix a problem before any penalty applies. Most citations are about overgrown yards, trash and vehicles.

  • Grass and weeds must stay under 7 inches.
  • Bring trash containers in from the curb on collection day; they may not go out more than 16 hours ahead of pickup.
  • Keep inoperable or unlicensed vehicles in a fully enclosed structure. No vehicle may park on grass.
  • Buildings, fences, retaining walls and sidewalks must be kept in good condition.

If the deadline in a compliance order lapses, the owner may face a General Ordinance Summons with fines from $100 to $500 that usually rise with repeat offenses. The city can also hire a contractor to board a structure or clear trash and weeds and add administrative costs, or tow vehicles at the owner's expense. Report problems or ask questions at codes@indepmo.org. Anyone who owns property in Independence and wants to bid at Jackson County's Delinquent Land Tax Sale must first request a Code Compliance Verification, which the city emails within two business days.

sections.h2: Can I run a short-term rental in Independence?
sections.html:
Yes, with a Short-Term Rental Permit approved by the Planning Commission. No new short-term rental may sit within 500 feet of an existing one, so call 816-325-7823 to check your address before applying.

The application requires an evacuation plan, a floor plan and a parking plan, plus a fee paid online. Operators report and remit the transient guest tax to the city every month. A buyer who plans to run a short-term rental should ask the city whether an existing permit transfers with the house.

sections.h2: Taxes and recording across the Jackson and Clay county line
sections.html:
Your parcel's county decides who bills the tax and records the deed, and most Independence addresses are in Jackson County. If your property sits in the small Clay County portion, the Clay County Collector and Recorder of Deeds handle it.

Real estate tax in Jackson County is billed once a year and is due December 31. The postmark counts, so a check postmarked December 29 is on time. Assessment ratios differ by use: 19% for residential, 32% for commercial and 12% for agricultural land.

Recording a deed at the Jackson County Recorder of Deeds starts at $23 for page one. Estate sellers often need a certified death certificate copy, which is $20. A state or federal tax lien is $3. Individual personal property is handled at the Truman Courthouse, 112 W. Lexington, on the first floor in Independence. Real property valuation is at 1300 Washington Street in Kansas City.

Independence falls within four public school districts: Independence, Blue Springs, Fort Osage and Raytown. Which district your street belongs to matters to buyers, so confirm it before you list. Independence has three public high schools and four public middle schools, among them Bridger, Pioneer Ridge, Bingham and Nowlin. Blue River Community College and a Graceland University campus are in the city.

Independence Power and Light, a city-owned electric utility founded in 1901, serves customers in town.

An agent listing fits a house in good repair. A direct cash sale fits a house with deferred work, a tenant, or an estate that needs a quick close, because the buyer takes the house as it stands and you skip showings and repair requests. Get any offer in writing and ask who pays closing costs.

Before you accept, check three things: which county bills your tax, whether a rental license and inspection are current, and whether any code violation is open. Open violations and unpaid tax can slow a closing, so settle them first or tell the buyer up front. The title company handles the payoff, the proration and the deed recording. Bring your latest tax statement, mortgage payoff figure and any rental paperwork to the first conversation so a buyer can price the house quickly.

faqs.q: What do landlords need in Independence?
faqs.a: The city licenses and inspects them. Landlords need a business license and a Rental Ready inspection every two years at $100 per unit. Since January 1, 2026, a valid license is required before utilities can start for a tenant.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Independence property taxes?
faqs.a: Jackson County for most addresses and Clay County for the small portion of the city that extends into it. Check your tax statement to see which collector sent it.

faqs.q: What are the common code problems on an Independence house?
faqs.a: Tall grass over 7 inches, trash containers left at the curb, unlicensed vehicles parked outside and deteriorated fences or sidewalks. Fines for a summons range from $100 to $500.

faqs.q: Can I list my Independence house as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Only with a city permit approved by the Planning Commission, and no new rental may be within 500 feet of another. Operators remit transient guest tax monthly.
Slightly shrinking. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 121,675, which is 1.0% below the 2020 base of 122,954.
